overall_summary: A soft jobs report has sharply reduced rate-hike odds, driving Bitcoin toward sixty-five thousand as yields and the dollar slide. Heavy whale buying and solid ETF inflows reinforce the risk-on tone, while equities hit fresh records. A Lightning Network exploit is the main caution, but an urgent patch is already out.
key_points: Possible Hormuz reopen aids risk assets

items.title: Senate Starts CLARITY Act Process, Vote Delayed to September
items.summary: Senate Majority Leader Thune filed the motion to proceed on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act early Saturday after overnight sessions, setting up initial procedural votes right after the August recess. Full floor action missed the pre-recess window and now faces a crowded September calendar plus remaining fights over ethics rules, stablecoin yields, and illicit finance. Traders should watch closely because passage would clarify SEC-CFTC lines and unlock more institutional capital, but failure or further delay keeps regulatory overhang alive into midterms.
items.impact: Keeps regulatory catalyst alive but delays clarity, limiting near-term upside conviction

items.title: BTCPay Exploit Drains Lightning Nodes; Urgent Patch Out
items.summary: Attackers exploited a critical BTCPay Server vulnerability to steal LND macaroon credentials and empty Lightning channels on merchant and payment nodes. Victims including Foundation Devices and Citadel21 reported overnight drains; the project rushed version 2.4.2 and told operators to patch immediately or take servers offline and refresh credentials. This hits bitcoin payment infrastructure right after the Coldcard hardware issues, raising self-custody and software risk awareness even if spot Bitcoin price barely reacted.
items.impact: Erodes confidence in Lightning and self-hosted tools, potential short-term risk-off for bitcoin ecosystem plays

items.title: Weak Jobs Report Lifts Bitcoin Toward $65K as Hike Odds Fall
items.summary: July nonfarm payrolls dropped 23,000 against expectations of 80,000-plus gains, with big downward revisions to prior months. Bitcoin pushed above 65,000 as markets slashed September Fed hike odds and raised chances of rates staying on hold. Traders care because softer labor data supports easier liquidity conditions that have historically favored risk assets like crypto, though geopolitics and energy prices could still keep the Fed cautious ahead of CPI.
items.impact: Macro tailwind that reduces rate-hike pressure and supports tests of resistance near 65k

items.title: Whales Buy $1.2B BTC, ETFs Take $750M Amid Coldcard Moves
items.summary: Wallets holding 10 to 10,000 BTC accumulated over 20,000 coins worth about 1.2 billion dollars since late July while spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in roughly 755 million for the week. Separately, long-term holder supply dropped as around 210,000 BTC left older wallets, largely seen as custody rotation after the Coldcard firmware exploit rather than pure dumping. This combination of large-holder accumulation and institutional inflows provides a demand floor even as price chops below 65k.
items.impact: Strong on-chain and ETF bid that cushions downside and favors eventual break higher

items.title: Treasury Sanctions More Iran-Linked Crypto Exchanges
items.summary: OFAC expanded its crackdown by designating additional Iranian digital-asset exchanges including Shelbit and Aban Tether for allegedly helping the IRGC evade sanctions and move funds. This continues the administration's Economic Fury campaign targeting crypto rails used by Tehran. Traders should note it reinforces U.S. willingness to police crypto for national security, which can tighten compliance for global platforms while having limited direct effect on Bitcoin spot flows.
items.impact: Heightens regulatory and compliance scrutiny on exchanges without broad market sell pressure

items.title: Trump Media Scraps Crypto.com CRO Treasury Deals
items.summary: Trump Media and Technology Group mutually terminated its planned CRO treasury company and related services deals with Crypto.com and Yorkville, citing saturated digital-asset treasury markets and a pivot toward media and a fusion-energy merger. CRO sold off hard on the news. For Bitcoin traders this is mostly altcoin and narrative noise, but it shows cooling enthusiasm for celebrity or political token treasury vehicles after the boom.
items.impact: Negative for CRO and related tokens; minimal direct Bitcoin price impact

items.title: US July Payrolls Plunge 23k, Far Below Forecasts
items.summary: The Labor Department reported nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July versus expectations of around plus 80,000. Prior months were revised down by a combined 103,000, unemployment edged to 4.1 percent, and wage growth slowed to 0.1 percent month-over-month or 3.2 percent year-over-year. Traders should care because this cools the labor market narrative and sharply reduces odds of a near-term Fed rate hike, supporting risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Lower rate-hike odds boost liquidity-sensitive assets

items.title: Treasury Yields Drop as Jobs Data Cools Hike Bets
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell several basis points to around 4.60-4.65 percent and the 2-year dropped more after the weak payrolls print. Markets scaled back September Fed hike probability from near 55-58 percent to about 40-42 percent. Bond traders and crypto desks watch this closely because falling yields ease financial conditions and historically support Bitcoin prices.
items.impact: Easier financial conditions aid risk assets

items.title: US Dollar Index Slides After Soft Labor Report
items.summary: The DXY fell roughly 0.3 to 0.5 percent toward the mid-99s, nearing recent lows, as rate differentials narrowed on reduced hike expectations. A weaker dollar typically lifts dollar-priced commodities and crypto by improving global liquidity and risk appetite. Crypto traders monitor DXY closely as a key inverse correlation driver in the short term.
items.impact: Weaker dollar supportive for Bitcoin and risk

items.title: S&P 500 Hits Fresh Record on Faded Rate-Hike Fears
items.summary: Equities rallied with the S&P 500 closing at a new record, up about 0.6 percent, Nasdaq gaining over 1 percent, after the jobs miss reduced pressure for tighter policy. This risk-on move reflects relief that the Fed under Chair Warsh may stay on hold longer. Equity strength often spills into crypto via improved sentiment and liquidity.

items.title: NY Fed Nowcast Cut to 2.2 Percent for Q3 GDP
items.summary: The New York Fed staff nowcast for third-quarter growth dropped to 2.2 percent after the weak payrolls and related data more than offset other positives. This signals softer momentum heading into the back half of the year. Growth concerns can create two-way risk for markets, though the rate relief currently dominates trader focus.
items.impact: Softer growth offset by lower rate pressure

items.title: Markets Test Warsh Fed as Hike Odds Plunge
items.summary: The weak jobs data challenges new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's less-forward-guidance approach and market-led tightening preference, with September hike odds falling sharply. Inflation data next week including CPI will be pivotal for whether rates stay on hold. Crypto traders need to watch the evolving reaction function closely as policy uncertainty remains elevated.
items.impact: Policy uncertainty until next inflation prints

items.title: US Eyes Imminent Iran-Oman Deal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: A US official reported progress between Iran and Oman that could soon reopen the Strait of Hormuz, potentially restoring oil flows disrupted by the five-month US-Iran war. Temporary shipping lanes are under discussion without tolls, though full details and US approval remain pending. Traders should care because this waterway handles a huge share of global oil and LNG; reopening would ease the energy shock, lower oil prices, and support risk assets by cooling inflation fears.
items.impact: Potential drop in oil prices and risk-on relief for markets

items.title: Senate Passes Sweeping Russia Energy Sanctions Bill
items.summary: The US Senate voted 86-11 on Friday to pass the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, authorizing up to 100 percent tariffs on the top importers of Russian oil and gas such as China and India, plus measures against the shadow fleet. It now heads to the House after summer recess. This matters for traders because it threatens secondary sanctions that could disrupt global energy trade, raise costs, or pressure Moscow's war funding, adding volatility to oil and risk assets depending on enforcement.
items.impact: Heightened trade and energy market uncertainty pending House action

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan Sign Mutual Defense Pact
items.summary: Leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Friday, pledging that an armed attack on one counts as an attack on all. It comes amid the Iran war and Houthi threats to Gulf energy infrastructure. Crypto traders should watch this as it reshapes Middle East alliances among key US partners, potentially stabilizing oil producers or heightening regional confrontation risks that feed into energy prices and global risk sentiment.
items.impact: Possible shift in regional deterrence affecting oil supply security

items.title: Houthis Escalate Attacks on Saudi-Backed Forces and Threaten Kingdom
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthis launched fresh missile and drone strikes on Yemeni government positions in Marib and Hadramout, killing dozens, while intelligence warns of imminent coordinated attacks with Iraqi militias on Saudi energy sites, ports, and airports. This widens the Iran-related conflict. Traders care because strikes on Saudi infrastructure or shipping could spike oil prices further and hit risk assets through higher energy costs and geopolitical premium.
items.impact: Elevated oil price risk and broader Middle East escalation fears

items.title: Russia Suffers Record July Casualties as Ukraine Hits Refineries
items.summary: Ukraine claimed Russia took about 43,000 casualties in July, its highest monthly toll this year, while Moscow dropped a record number of glide bombs and ballistic missiles that are depleting Ukrainian air defenses. Ukraine continued deep drone strikes on major Russian oil refineries. This ongoing attrition war keeps energy and geopolitical risks elevated for markets, with potential further Russian oil disruptions adding to supply tightness already strained by the Iran conflict.
items.impact: Sustained energy supply risks and prolonged conflict drag

items.title: DRC Bans Copper and Cobalt Concentrate Exports
items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo announced a ban on exporting copper and cobalt concentrates to force more domestic processing, with the order publicized around August 6 after taking effect earlier. Copper prices jumped nearly two percent on the news. This hits global battery and electronics supply chains hard since the DRC dominates cobalt and is a top copper producer, raising input costs for tech hardware including mining gear and potentially feeding into broader inflation or commodity volatility relevant to risk assets.
items.impact: Upward pressure on industrial metals prices and supply-chain costs
